# Tsugumi

> Run the analysis you sketched with AI, as it is, and check it with your own hands.

Tsugumi is a research workbench in which the specification a person draws, the thing an AI edits and the processing that actually runs are one and the same Workflow. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows (checked on macOS and on Linux, Ubuntu and NixOS; on Windows, through WSL2, as far as opening a demo).
You draw a computation or a data pipeline as Cards and the wires between them, implement it together with an AI, and run it in environments pinned with Nix.
You open the code or the result of a Card you are curious about, change a condition and try again with the inputs that were saved. Going back and forth like this, a researcher comes to understand how the analysis got where it did, and can ask the next question.

The documents are written for both people and AI. The URLs below are the Markdown version of each page. How to check each claim is in "Claims and how to check them", with the code, tests and commands.

## Overview

- [README](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/index.md): the problem, how to use it, and the real screens explained

## Getting started

- [Installation and development builds](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/install.md): Installing and updating the desktop app and the `tsugumi` command (Mac, Linux, Windows), and building from source
- [Usage](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/usage.md): Getting started by following a demo's guide, and the operations you use most
- [Your first Card](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/cardguide.md): Your first Card: a Card that takes an input and computes, written in Python, bash, C++, R and Julia (a test runs the code on this page)
- [The bundled demos](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/demos.md): How the bundled demos work: how each demo's Cards connect, what each Card does, and what to try
- [Web UI](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/webui.md): The same screens in the browser (the `tsugumi` command: the shared VM on a Mac, bubblewrap on Linux, WSL on Windows)
- [Using it from Claude Code](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/claude-code.md): Having Claude Code make and run Cards through the Claude Code plugin, shown in the Web UI

## The ideas

- [What to build so that we are not used by AI](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/philosophy.md): "What to build so that we are not used by AI": the concern behind Tsugumi, where it started, its name, how it was built and its author
- [Why one Workflow for design, implementation and checking](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/rationale.md): Why design, implementation and checking share one Workflow: answers to the three reasons for hesitating to hand research to AI (an invisible process, reproducibility, data), the measures that keep trial and error light, and where to check each
- [Vision and applications](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/vision.md): Applications: learning research decisions, growing tools, handing work to the next person, and the idea of business automation
- [Plans and guarantees](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/limitations.md): The current scope, plans and the scope of the guarantees

## How it works

- [Tsugumi's features](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/features.md): A technical tour of the main features (architecture, Cards and Workflows, Nix, SDK and workers, saving, history, visualisation, UI, Agent, demos)
- [Versions (git)](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/versions.md): Versions: the project's git, each run's version and result (git notes), the version tree and "Start from This Version"
- [Security and isolation](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/security.md): What is and is not protected, the four isolation boundaries (VM, project, Card, RPC), API keys, where data is kept, and known limitations
- [The RPC contract](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/protocol.md): The RPC contract: the 41 requests and the notifications (generated from `protocol/tsugumi.fbs`)
- [Glossary](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/glossary.md): Card, Draft, Run, invocation, version and other terms

## Records and development

- [Claims and how to check them](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/evidence.md): How to check each claim: test names, commands and the last environment checked, and a run with the real Claude API
- [Development](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/development.md): Design decisions of the runtime, tests and what has been checked, measurements, implementation status

## Repository

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gen740/Tsugumi/main/AGENTS.md): a map, the claims and where to check them, and instructions for agents working in this repository
- [The Card specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gen740/Tsugumi/main/agent/Reference/card-guide.md): the same document the app's Agent reads
- [The RPC contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gen740/Tsugumi/main/protocol/tsugumi.fbs): the source of the contract the UI, the Web and the Agent use

## Optional

- [Pinned versions](https://gen740.github.io/Tsugumi/pages/lock.md): Pinned versions of the runtime and its dependencies
